attribution: Author unknown; presented as a dialogue between Shiva and the Goddess
period: Generally placed in the early to middle second millennium CE; dates are uncertain
summary: A major scripture of the Kaula tantric tradition, covering the guru, initiation, ritual and the philosophy behind Kaula practice.
whyRead: It is an important source for Kaula Tantra, and especially for the tantric doctrine of the guru. It shows Tantra as an integrated system of theology, ethics, ritual and contemplation, not a collection of techniques.
questions: What is the role of the guru?
How can worldly experience become part of a liberating path?

keyTeachings.title: The Kaula path
keyTeachings.text: The text presents the Kaula path as the highest, one that aims at both enjoyment (bhukti) and liberation (mukti) rather than opposing them.

keyTeachings.title: The guru
keyTeachings.text: Several chapters treat the guru as a form of Shiva and set out the qualities of a true teacher and disciple.

keyTeachings.title: Initiation and ritual
keyTeachings.text: Initiation, mantra and worship, including rites involving substances normally prohibited, are to be undertaken only within a qualified lineage and with ethical discipline; the text warns against their misuse.

keyTeachings.title: Rarity of human birth
keyTeachings.text: It opens by stressing the value of human birth as an opportunity for liberation.

structure.label: Seventeen chapters (ullasas) in the common edition

relatedTexts.note: A more contemplative Tantra of the Bhairava tradition
